caption: The drawing depicts a top-down view of a geometric garden layout bordered by a river on the right side and a path lined with trees on the left side. The garden is divided into four main rectangular sections, each filled with symmetrical, ornamental pathways and planting beds colored in shades of green, pink, and tan. There are two main paths intersecting at right angles, lined with evenly spaced trees, and several secondary paths within each section, creating intricate patterns. Adjacent to the garden, along the lower edge, are three red-roofed rectangular buildings located near the garden’s entrance. The surrounding landscape is painted in various tones of green representing lawns and trees, with a sandy beige area at the bottom, possibly denoting a riverbank, and a blue curved river flowing alongside the right edge of the scene. Scattered around the edges of the garden and alongside the paths are individual trees depicted as small green circles or cone shapes. To the far left, the path curves from top to bottom, lined with evenly spaced trees, and the river curves gently at the lower right corner.
title: Corlaer Estate and Garden
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
